subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden NO_REPLY handling beyond token-only, punctuation-wrapped, reasoning-prefixed, and cron-path cases to suppress generic non-empty text followed by the token?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves generic substantive trailing-token replies, while the issue asks for broader suppression to prevent internal text leaks; that security-versus-message-loss boundary needs maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Adopt a shared silent-intent classifier
options.body: Suppress internal or heartbeat/private-summary mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies that only mention or append NO_REPLY.

options.title: Suppress any trailing or contained token
options.body: Treat any response containing or ending in NO_REPLY as silent and accept compatibility risk from dropped visible text.

options.title: Keep current targeted rules
options.body: Document the current narrow policy and close or retarget broad suppress-if-present requests to explicit product discussion.

recommendation.title: Adopt a shared silent-intent classifier
recommendation.body: Suppress internal or heartbeat/private-summary mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies that only mention or append NO_REPLY.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current maintainer-facing routing candidate from recent silent-reply hardening and release history around this shared behavior.
